## Slice 10 (Overdue Category Invoicing + Dashboard KPI Freshness) — 2026-08-04

**Verdict: both bug fixes from the approved plan (`tidy-puzzling-snowflake.md`) are built and verified live end-to-end.** Fix 1: `BulkAdhocInvoicesService.generateForStudent()` now clamps a matched structure line's effective due date to `max(line.dueDate, today)` before grouping, so a category whose real due date has already passed generates an invoice due today instead of throwing and landing that student in `failed[]`. Fix 2: `DashboardKpisService.getTodaysCollection()` now computes LIVE against `pay_receipt`/`pay_receipt_split` instead of reading the possibly-stale `mv_daily_collections`, and the dashboard page now fires `useRefreshDashboard()` once on mount, gating the still-MV-backed KPI tiles (Outstanding Fees, Defaulters, Revenue/Expense/Surplus, Wallet Liability) behind that refresh's completion — with graceful degradation on a genuine refresh failure, which turned out to be exercised for real, not just theoretically (see the honestly-flagged pre-existing MV-ownership gap below). A real, necessary side-fix was also required and made: `<QueryBoundary>`'s state resolution had a genuine bug (`isLoading` instead of `isPending`) that would have shown every newly-gated KPI tile as "empty" instead of "loading" during the gating window — found and fixed as part of making Fix 2's gating actually work correctly, not a separate, unscoped change.

### Fix 1 — overdue category invoicing (`packages/server/src/domains/billing/application/bulk-adhoc-invoices.service.ts`)

Read `invoicing.service.ts`'s `generateInvoice()` first, per the dispatch's own explicit instruction, to confirm the real enforcement mechanism before writing anything: `dueDate >= issueDate` (`ck_bill_invoice_due_after_issue`) is enforced at the **TypeScript service level** (`if (dueDate < issueDate) throw new ValidationException(...)`, `invoicing.service.ts:197`), not only a DB CHECK constraint — confirmed by reading the code directly, not assumed. "Today" is computed the same way this exact codebase already does it everywhere else for this purpose: `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` (`invoicing.service.ts:195`, and independently confirmed as the same convention `InvoicesController`'s own `todayIsoDate()` and several reports already use).

**The fix**: in `generateForStudent()`, immediately before the existing `groupsByDueDate` grouping loop, each matched line's EFFECTIVE due date is now computed as `line.dueDate < today ? today : line.dueDate` (plain ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string comparison — lexical comparison is correct for this format, matching `generateInvoice()`'s own `dueDate < issueDate` check exactly), and grouping now happens on the effective date, not the raw one. Two already-past-due categories with DIFFERENT original due dates now collapse into ONE invoice due today; a category with a genuine future due date is completely unaffected and still groups separately. The method's doc comment (previously titled "Known interaction, not worked around" and explicitly stating the OPPOSITE of the new behavior) was rewritten to describe the real clamping behavior and why: an already-passed one-time-fee due date shouldn't block billing at all — it's due immediately instead, which correctly lands the resulting invoice in the "Upcoming" bucket (`due_date >= today`, Slice 8 Part 2's own bucketing rule), not silently dropped to `failed[]`.

This fixes BOTH real entry points, since both already share this one service: the bulk "Generate Invoice" screen (`POST billing/invoices/bulk-generate` with multiple `studentIds`) and the redesigned per-student dialog (Slice 9 Part D — the SAME endpoint with `studentIds:[studentId]`).

**Tests** (`bulk-adhoc-invoices.service.spec.ts`, +3, now 8 total): the file's `beforeEach` now uses `jest.useFakeTimers()` + `jest.setSystemTime(new Date("2026-07-15T00:00:00Z"))` (matching `numbering.service.spec.ts`'s own established fake-timer pattern) — a fixed "today" chosen before every pre-existing fixture due date (`2026-08-01`/`2026-09-01`) so those 5 tests' own assertions stay byte-for-byte valid unmodified, with `afterEach(() => jest.useRealTimers())`. New `describe("past-due-date clamping (Slice 10)")` block: (a) a single matched line with a past due date (`2026-06-01`) → clamped to today (`2026-07-15`), `succeeded[]` not `failed[]`; (b) two matched lines with different past due dates (`2026-05-01`/`2026-06-10`) → collapse into exactly ONE invoice due today, `generateInvoice()` called once with both lines' `adhocLines`; (c) one past-due line (`2026-06-01`) + one genuine future-due line (`2026-09-01`) in the same call → TWO separate invoices, due dates `["2026-07-15","2026-09-01"]`, confirmed NOT merged.

### Fix 2 — dashboard KPI freshness (`packages/server/src/domains/reporting/application/dashboard-kpis.service.ts`, `apps/web/src/app/(erp)/dashboard/page.tsx`, `apps/web/src/hooks/use-dashboard.ts`)

**Backend — `getTodaysCollection()` now live, a real deviation from the plan's own suggested location, made after reading the actual established convention, not before**: the plan suggested adding a new method to `PayReceiptRepository` (in `domains/payments`) and calling it from `DashboardKpisService`. Before doing that, `materialized-views.repository.ts` and `pay-receipt.repository.ts` were read as instructed — but so was `module-deps.json`'s own `domains/reporting` entry, which EXPLICITLY documents this module's established, deliberate convention for this exact data need: *"domains/payments — fee-collection.report.ts/receipts-register.report.ts/DashboardKpisService.getCollectionRate() read pay_receipt/pay_receipt_split (raw DataSource.query() joins... entity types not imported — only table names, so no entity-level FK is added)"*. `getCollectionRate()`, in this SAME file, already computes an almost-identical `SUM(pay_receipt_split.amount)` for `POSTED` receipts in a date range this exact way. Adding a new `PayReceiptRepository` method and importing `PaymentsModule` into `ReportingModule` for DI would have worked (nothing in `module-deps.json` forbids it — `domains/payments` is already in reporting's `mayImport` list) but would have been a materially bigger, architecturally-inconsistent footprint than this file's own already-proven raw-SQL precedent for the identical shape of query. **Deviation, made deliberately and documented inline on the method itself**: `getTodaysCollection()` now runs `SELECT COALESCE(SUM(s.amount),0)::text AS total FROM app.pay_receipt r JOIN app.pay_receipt_split s ON s.receipt_id = r.id WHERE r.status = 'POSTED' AND r.receipt_date = $1` via the existing `@InjectDataSource() dataSource` the class already had — no new repository method, no new constructor dependency, no new NestJS module import. The method's own signature/return shape (`{date, total: Money}`) is byte-for-byte unchanged, so `DashboardController.todaysCollection()` needed zero changes (only its `@ApiOperation` summary text was corrected — it still said "(mv_daily_collections)"). Every OTHER KPI method (`getOutstandingFees`/`getRevenueExpenseSurplus`/`getWalletLiability`/`getDefaultersCount`/`listTopDefaulters`) is completely untouched, still MV-backed, per the plan's explicit scope. `mv-daily-collections.view-entity.ts`'s own doc comment (which claimed the MV fed "Today's Collection... and trend chart") was also corrected to reflect it now only feeds the trend chart.

**Tests** (`dashboard-kpis.service.spec.ts`): the old `getTodaysCollection` test (which mocked `mvRepository.findDailyCollections()`) was replaced with two new tests confirming (1) the live query path — `mvRepository.findDailyCollections` is never called, `dataSource.query()` is called with SQL containing `pay_receipt_split`/`r.status = 'POSTED'`/`r.receipt_date = $1` and params `[today]`; (2) a zero-result live query correctly returns a zero total. Every other test in the file (`getOutstandingFees`/`getRevenueExpenseSurplus`/`getWalletLiability`/`getDefaultersCount`/`listTopDefaulters`/`getCollectionTrendChart`/`getCashFlow`) is unchanged.

**Frontend — mount-refresh + gating (`dashboard/page.tsx`)**: `useRefreshDashboard()`'s mutation now fires once on mount via a `useRef` guard (`hasFiredMountRefreshRef`, the exact same "run exactly once" pattern `collect-fees-flow.tsx`'s own `appliedInitialStudentRef`/`appliedInitialInvoiceRef` already established for React StrictMode's dev-only double-invoke of mount effects), inside a `React.useEffect(() => {...}, [])` with an explicit `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` (matching `academic-year-term-select.tsx`'s own established precedent for this exact suppression). `mvKpisReady = refreshMutation.isSuccess || refreshMutation.isError` gates `useOutstandingFees`/`useRevenueExpenseSurplus`/`useWalletLiability`/`useDefaultersCount`/`useTopDefaulters` via a new, additive `options?: {enabled?: boolean}` second parameter on each hook (`use-dashboard.ts`, same shape `useStudents()`'s own `options.enabled` precedent from Slice 8 Part 1) — deliberately `isSuccess || isError`, NOT `isSuccess` alone, so a genuine refresh failure still lets the KPI queries fire against whatever the MVs already hold, rather than blocking the page forever. `useTodaysCollection()` (now live), `useCollectionRate()` (confirmed via its own doc comment to already be a live ledger query, not MV-backed), and `useCollectionTrend()`/`useCashFlow()`/`useIncomeVsExpense()` (MV-backed but a 30-day/90-day historical series, where page-load-triggered freshness is fine per the plan's own explicit scope boundary) are deliberately NOT gated. The existing manual "Refresh data" button is completely unchanged — same `refreshMutation.mutate()` call.

**A real, necessary bug found and fixed in `query-boundary.tsx`, not a separate unscoped change**: TanStack Query v5 defines `isLoading = isPending && isFetching` (confirmed by reading `@tanstack/query-core`'s own compiled `queryObserver.js` directly, not assumed) — a query that is `enabled: false` and has never fetched has `isPending: true` but `isFetching: false`, so `isLoading` is FALSE for it. `resolveQueryBoundaryState()`'s old `isLoading`-based check therefore fell through to the `data === undefined` branch and misreported every newly-gated KPI query as `"empty"` ("No data found") for the entire gating window on every single dashboard page load — a real, visible regression this fix would otherwise have shipped. Fixed by switching the check to `query.isPending` (TanStack's own general "do I have data yet" flag, covering both "actively fetching" and "gated/not enabled yet") — the more correct general implementation, not a special case. This required widening `QueryBoundaryProps<T>["query"]`'s `Pick<...>` type from `"isLoading"` to `"isPending"`, which surfaced two other call sites that hand-build a query-shaped object rather than passing a raw `useQuery()` result: `app/(erp)/students/page.tsx` (`activeQuery.isLoading` → `activeQuery.isPending`) and `features/students/hooks/use-guardians.ts`'s `useStudentGuardians()` (its combined `isLoading: linksQuery.isLoading || guardiansQuery.isLoading` → `isPending: linksQuery.isPending || guardiansQuery.isPending`) — both fixed, both re-confirmed clean under `tsc`/lint.

**i18n**: no new keys added — the existing `queryBoundary.loadingTitle` a11y copy (already present, already wired into every `<QueryBoundary>` loading state) now correctly renders during the gating window once the `isPending` fix above landed, satisfying the plan's own "reuse existing loading-state patterns" option. `en`/`sw`/`fr.json` were not edited — re-confirmed all three still parse as valid JSON, identical top-level key sets, identical 1306 lines each (unchanged from Slice 9 Part B/C/D).

**Contracts regen: skipped, as the plan anticipated** — `getTodaysCollection()`'s return shape (`{date, total}`) is byte-for-byte unchanged, and no DTO/route was added or altered for either fix (Fix 1 touched only `bulk-adhoc-invoices.service.ts`'s internal grouping logic, already-existing DTOs untouched). No `openapi.json`/`openapi-types.ts`/`*.schema.ts` regeneration was needed or performed.

**A real, pre-existing, out-of-scope gap found during live verification, flagged not fixed**: `POST dashboard/refresh-mvs` (the manual "Refresh data" button's own endpoint, and now also this dispatch's new mount-refresh mutation) returns a real `500` — `"must be owner of materialized view mv_daily_collections"`. Direct `psql` cross-check: `SELECT matviewowner FROM pg_matviews WHERE schemaname='app'` → all 5 views owned by `kfe_migrate`; `SELECT current_user` from the same connection profile `apps/api` itself uses → `kfe_app` (the DML-only APP role, per `AppModule`'s own doc comment — deliberately never `kfe_migrate` at app boot). `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` requires the executing role to own the view; no `GRANT` was ever issued anywhere in this codebase's migrations (confirmed by grep across every migration file) giving `kfe_app` that privilege — this gap has existed since migration `0160` first created these views, completely unrelated to either of this dispatch's own source-code changes (neither Fix 1 nor Fix 2 touches `MvRefreshService`, `MaterializedViewsRepository.refresh()`, or any migration). Attempting the `GRANT` directly as `kfe_app` correctly no-ops (`WARNING: no privileges were granted` — `kfe_app` isn't the owner and has no `GRANT OPTION`, confirming this can't be self-healed by the app role). Out of this dispatch's explicit scope (a DB role/GRANT fix, not a bug in either Fix 1 or Fix 2's own code) — flagged here for whoever next touches `MvRefreshService`/Module 18's ops story, matching this codebase's own established "flag, don't silently expand scope" precedent (Slice 8 Part 3's BANK_TRANSFER FK finding). **This gap is exactly why the mount-refresh gating's `isSuccess || isError` (not `isSuccess`-only) design decision matters in practice, not just in theory**: in this real dev environment, the mount-refresh mutation genuinely fails every time, and the gated KPI queries correctly still fire anyway (verified: `getOutstandingFees()` etc. read the MVs via plain `SELECT`, which needs no ownership, only the `SELECT` grant `kfe_app` already has for every `app` schema table — confirmed live, `mv_ar_summary` returned 9 real rows).

## Slice 10 follow-up — `refresh-mvs` ownership fix — 2026-08-05

Closes the one gap the Slice 10 write-up above deliberately left open: `POST /dashboard/refresh-mvs` (the dashboard's "Refresh data" button) was a real, silent `500` ("must be owner of materialized view mv_daily_collections") from the moment migration `0160` first created these 5 views — `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` requires the connecting role to OWN the view (unlike `SELECT`, ownership can't be granted separately), but every view under `app.*` is owned by `kfe_migrate` (the DDL-only migration role) while the app connects at runtime as `kfe_app` (DML-only).

**Two approaches were weighed before choosing**: (a) transfer ownership of the 5 views to `kfe_app`, or (b) a `SECURITY DEFINER` database function/procedure letting `kfe_app` trigger a refresh without owning anything, more strictly preserving the DML-only/DDL-only role separation `migration-0190`'s own doc comment establishes ("kfe_app has no license.* access... narrow grants, not ownership transfers"). Approach (b) was rejected: `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY` cannot run inside a transaction block, and a plain function body always executes within its caller's implicit transaction — a `SECURITY DEFINER` PROCEDURE with an internal `COMMIT` before the refresh might work around this, but that could not be verified empirically against a real Postgres instance in this environment (a direct test was correctly blocked as a sensitive, unreviewed DDL action) — shipping an unverified transaction-control workaround for a role-security-relevant migration was judged worse than the narrower, guaranteed-correct alternative. Approach (a) was chosen and confirmed, with the user's explicit go-ahead, as a genuinely narrow exception rather than a real privilege widening: these 5 views are pure read-model aggregates over tables `kfe_app` already has full DML on (`pay_receipt`, `bill_invoice`, `wal_wallet`, ...) — owning the derived views grants no data access `kfe_app` didn't already have, only the ability to re-run the `SELECT` that already defines each one.

New migration `packages/server/src/migrations/0231-transfer-reporting-mv-ownership-to-app-role.ts` — `ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW app.{view} OWNER TO kfe_app` for all 5 `REPORTING_MATERIALIZED_VIEW_NAMES`, idempotent, with a `down()` reverting to `kfe_migrate`. Run for real via `pnpm run migration:run` (from `packages/server`) — confirmed executed against the live dev DB, `TransferReportingMvOwnershipToAppRole1700000000231` recorded in `app.typeorm_migrations`.

**Verification**: `SELECT matviewname, matviewowner FROM pg_matviews WHERE schemaname='app'` — all 5 now show `kfe_app`. The actual operation that was failing — `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY app.{view}`, run as `kfe_app` — now succeeds cleanly for all 5 views (previously the exact "must be owner" error). `pnpm --filter server exec tsc --noEmit` clean. `pnpm --filter server exec jest reporting --maxWorkers=2` → 26 suites, 81 tests, all passing (no regression from the ownership change). `apps/api` restarted to pick up the new migration state.

## Slice 10 correction — preserve the real fee-structure due date, don't clamp — 2026-08-05

The Slice 10 "overdue category invoicing" fix above was itself wrong in a way the user caught live: clamping a past-due structure line's effective due date up to today made generation succeed, but it silently changed the invoice's `due_date` away from what the fee structure actually configures — real data loss, not a cosmetic issue. The user's own words: "maintain the original due date set in the fee structure."

**Root cause of why clamping seemed necessary in the first place**: `ck_bill_invoice_due_after_issue` (`CHECK (due_date >= issue_date)`, migration `0070`) plus a matching TypeScript guard in `InvoicingService.generateInvoice()` (`if (dueDate < issueDate) throw ValidationException(...)`). Neither had a documented business-rule reference — unlike every genuinely load-bearing invariant `0070`'s own doc comment names, this one read as a generic sanity guard, not a deliberate rule.

**Why `issue_date` itself can't be backdated instead** (the other way to reconcile "keep the real due date" with the old constraint): `issue_date` is not a free label — it's the invoice's real GL journal posting date (`invoicing.service.ts`'s own `journalDate: invoice.issueDate`), and `PostingService.post()` requires an OPEN `gl_period` covering that date, rejecting `HARD_CLOSED` ones (`posting.service.ts:280-286`, confirmed by reading it directly). Backdating `issueDate` to match an old due date would trade one error for a much less predictable one — "no gl_period covers this date" or "period HARD_CLOSED" — for any category due more than a few months back. `issue_date` correctly stays "today."

**The real fix**: drop the constraint (and its TS-level mirror) outright, and revert the clamping — due dates are now grouped and stored EXACTLY as configured on the fee structure line, even when that's in the past relative to `issue_date`. Confirmed before dropping it that nothing else in the codebase assumes `due_date >= issue_date` (every consumer found — `debit-notes.service.ts`, `late-fee-batches.service.ts`, `invoices-register.report.ts`, Pending/Upcoming bucketing, aging reports — reads `due_date` alone, comparing it to `balance`/`CURRENT_DATE`, never to `issue_date`).

**Changes**:
- New migration `packages/server/src/migrations/0232-drop-bill-invoice-due-after-issue-check.ts` — `ALTER TABLE app.bill_invoice DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS ck_bill_invoice_due_after_issue`, idempotent, `down()` restores it. Run for real via `pnpm run migration:run`.
- `bill-invoice.entity.ts` — the matching `@Check("ck_bill_invoice_due_after_issue", ...)` decorator removed, so the entity stays honest about the real DB schema.
- `invoicing.service.ts`'s `generateInvoice()` — the `if (dueDate < issueDate) throw` guard removed; `dueDate` still defaults to `issueDate` when omitted (unchanged), but no longer rejects an explicitly-supplied past date.
- `bulk-adhoc-invoices.service.ts`'s `generateForStudent()` — reverted to grouping matched lines by each line's own REAL `dueDate` (no `max(line.dueDate, today)` clamp); class doc comment rewritten to describe the corrected behavior and why.
- `bulk-adhoc-invoices.service.spec.ts` — the "past-due-date clamping" describe block replaced with 4 tests asserting the due date is preserved exactly: a single past-due line, two lines sharing the identical past due date (still one invoice), two lines with DIFFERENT past due dates (now genuinely two separate invoices, not merged), and a mixed past+future case. The now-unnecessary `jest.useFakeTimers()`/`setSystemTime` scaffolding (only needed for the old clamp's `new Date()` read) was removed.
- `pending-upcoming-invoices.integration.spec.ts` — a stale comment corrected (its fixed `issueDate="2000-01-01"` was never strictly REQUIRED by the now-dropped constraint, just kept for fixture realism).

**Verification — real, live, against the running stack**: `pnpm --filter server exec tsc --noEmit` clean. `pnpm --filter server exec jest billing --maxWorkers=2` → 19 suites, 183 tests, all passing (up from 179 — the 4 rewritten tests replace the old 3). `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` → 4/4 clean (no frontend files touched by this fix). Migration `0232` confirmed applied (`DropBillInvoiceDueAfterIssueCheck1700000000232` in `app.typeorm_migrations`); `SELECT conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid='app.bill_invoice'::regclass AND conname='ck_bill_invoice_due_after_issue'` → 0 rows.

Real end-to-end proof via a throwaway `apps/api/src/verify-followup.ts` (`NestFactory.createApplicationContext`, real `InvoicingService.generateInvoice()`/`.postInvoice()` calls against the live DB, deleted immediately after use — `apps/api/src/` confirmed back to its 3 original files): generated a real ADHOC invoice with an explicit `dueDate:"2026-06-01"` (genuinely in the past relative to the real `issueDate:"2026-08-04"` this ran against) — **all 4 real assertions passed**: `invoice.dueDate === "2026-06-01"` (not clamped), `invoice.status === "POSTED"` (generation + posting both succeeded, no throw), a direct DB read confirms `due_date="2026-06-01"`, and confirms `due_date < issue_date` — the exact state the old constraint used to forbid, now proven to work end-to-end. The throwaway invoice (`BIL-000136`) was voided as real cleanup.

Dev servers: `apps/api` rebuilt and restarted (old PID 32848 → new PID 19788) to pick up the dropped constraint and reverted service logic; `apps/worker`/`apps/web` untouched. All three confirmed healthy afterward, 7 `node.exe` processes (standard steady state), no orphaned verification-script processes left behind.

### Next action

None. Both the original Slice 10 fix and this correction are complete — invoices for a category whose due date has passed now generate successfully AND preserve the real configured due date.

## Slice 11 (Part 3 — Wallet: Approval-Gated Transactions, Service Points, Reconciliation) — 2026-08-05

**Verdict: all three real two-step approval dances (transfer, refund, adjust), Service Points CRUD + operator assignment, on-demand Reconciliation, and the `EntityLabel` extension are built and verified genuinely end-to-end against the live stack** — real threshold-gated direct/needs-approval branching, a real submit→decide→execute round trip through the actual Approvals inbox engine (two real users, a submitter and a decider, since BR-APPR-01 blocks self-approval), and direct `psql` cross-checks of every resulting balance/row. No backend changes — every endpoint already existed, confirmed by reading `wallet-transactions.controller.ts`/`instances.controller.ts`/`service-points.controller.ts`/`reconciliation.controller.ts` in full first, per the dispatch's own instruction. **No contracts regen needed** — confirmed explicitly: every DTO/type used already existed in `@klickit/contracts` (the `domains_wallet_wallet_transaction_schema` namespace already carried `TransferToWalletDto`/`RefundWalletDto`/`AdjustWalletDto`/`WalletApprovalRequestResponseDto`/`TransferToWalletResponseDto` from Part 2's own regen; `service-point.schema.ts`'s DTOs are flatly exported with no name collisions).

### A real, confirmed backend DTO-reuse validation gap, found by live-probing before writing any UI

Live-probed `POST /wallets/:id/refund/request`/`POST /wallets/:id/adjust/request` with only `{amount}` BEFORE assuming their shape: both genuinely reject with a real `400` (`RefundWalletDto`/`AdjustWalletDto` are the SAME class the execute endpoints use, and the global `ValidationPipe` — `whitelist:true`, no `skipMissingProperties`, confirmed in `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` — enforces every `@IsUUID()`/`@IsIn()`-decorated field as required even though `requestRefund()`/`requestAdjust()` only ever read `dto.amount`, confirmed by reading both handlers directly). Worked around on the frontend only (no backend change, out of scope): the REQUEST dialogs collect the real intended `payoutMethod`/`payoutTarget`/`direction`/`reasonCode` up front (genuinely useful — describes what's being asked for) and send a random `crypto.randomUUID()` as a format-satisfying `approvalRef` placeholder, proven live to be never read server-side for that call. Documented in `wallets.api.ts`'s own doc comment for whoever next does a DTO-hygiene pass.

### A second real, confirmed gap found while designing the "complete pending transfer/refund/adjustment" UX

`appr_instance` has no "consumed" flag anywhere (confirmed by reading `appr-instance.entity.ts`/`approval-engine.service.ts` directly) — an APPROVED instance stays APPROVED forever, and the execute endpoints never check the submitted amount against the instance's own approved `amount` either. `use-wallet-approvals.ts`'s `alreadyExecuted` works around this on the frontend by cross-referencing the wallet's own transaction ledger for a `wall_transaction.approval_ref` matching the latest instance id, hiding the "Complete" action once one is found — a real, honest UX fix for a genuine backend gap, not silently ignored.

## Slice 11 — closing summary (Parts 1–4 complete)

Phase 6 Slice 11 completed Modules 2 (Settings), 11 (Wallet), and 19 (Integrations) on the frontend — every backend endpoint across all three modules already existed from Phase 5; this slice was, across all 4 parts, almost entirely a frontend build, with exactly one small, necessary backend addition (`GET /wallets`, Part 2).

- **Settings** (Part 1): Academic Calendar (year/term management, set-current, billing-lock), Numbering Series (read-only list + preview-next), Custom Field Definitions (create/edit, entity-scoped) — plus the Settings nav entry's conversion from a flat link into a `children`-bearing dropdown.
- **Wallet** (Parts 2–3): a brand-new `/wallet` area from a 2-file stub — searchable paginated list, full detail page (top-up/spend/set-status/update-limits/close), student-page wallet card, then approval-gated transfer-to-fees/transfer-to-wallet (real threshold-driven direct-vs-submit-for-approval branching) and always-approval-required refund/adjust, Service Points CRUD + operator assignment, on-demand Reconciliation, and 3 new `EntityLabel` branches in the Approvals inbox — plus a new top-level Wallet nav dropdown grown to 3 children.
- **Integrations** (Part 4, this section): Module 2's Integrations page genuinely extended to configure QuickBooks/Xero/Sage (not just M-Pesa) via real per-kind branching logic; Module 19's first frontend surface — webhook subscriptions (full lifecycle: create/edit/rotate-secret/disable/enable) + deliveries (paginated, filterable, manual retry/process-due, no scheduler anywhere) + accounting-sync (a real, distinct-from-Module-2 Test Connection, plus a paginated/filterable sync log viewer) — plus the Settings dropdown's 2 final children, completing it at 6.

All 4 parts, across every dispatch's own live verification: real HTTP round trips against the running `apps/api`, direct `psql` cross-checks of every resulting DB row (money/state changes always independently confirmed, never taken on faith from an API response alone), real SSR route checks with no error markers, and — consistently, honestly flagged every single time — no browser automation tool was ever available across the whole slice, so real dialog-interaction UX (clicking, typing, watching a chip picker render) rests on code review plus the exact request/response shapes those components are proven to call, not on having watched a browser render them. `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` was clean at the end of every one of the 4 parts. All three dev servers (`apps/api` 3000, `apps/worker` 3001, `apps/web` 3002) are healthy as of this final part, with the standard 7 `node.exe` processes and nothing extra left running.

## Slice 11 follow-up — Wallet card empty-body bug + Academic Calendar search — 2026-08-05

Two small, real fixes found in actual use after Slice 11 shipped, both applied directly (no dispatch needed, small and well-understood).

**Bug 1 — student page's Wallet card showed "Couldn't load this / data is undefined" for every student with no wallet yet.** Root cause: `findWalletByStudent()` (`apps/web/src/features/wallet/api/wallets.api.ts`) never coerced an empty-body response to `null` — `WalletsController.findByStudent()` returns `wallet ? toView(wallet) : null`, and per the SAME confirmed behavior `features/payments/api/sessions.api.ts`'s `getMySession()` already documents: NestJS sends a genuinely EMPTY body for a `null` return (not the JSON text `"null"`), which `openapi-fetch` resolves to `undefined`, not `null` — tripping TanStack Query's own guard against a queryFn resolving to `undefined`. `WalletCard` itself was already correctly built to expect `wallet: WalletResponseDto | null` and render a real "Create wallet" branch for `null` — the bug was purely that `null` never actually arrived. Fixed identically to `getMySession()`'s own established fix: `const data = await unwrapApiResult<WalletResponseDto | undefined>(...); return data ?? null;` at the one call site that knows this endpoint's specific empty-body-means-null contract.

**Feature — search field on the Academic Calendar page.** Academic years have no separate numeric "year" field distinct from their own `name` (e.g. "2026", "AY 2026/27" are both valid real `name` values in this dev DB) — searching by name covers "search by name or year" in one field. A plain client-side `.filter()` over the already-fully-fetched years list (`useAcademicYears()` has no pagination concept, matching the same "small unbounded list" shape `student-selection-grid.tsx`'s own Slice 9 Part B precedent already established for an analogous case) — a debounce isn't needed since there's no network round trip. New `searchYearsPlaceholder`/`noYearsMatchSearch` i18n keys added identically to en/sw/fr (1971 lines each, up from 1969, valid JSON, matching key sets).

**Verification**: `pnpm --filter web exec tsc --noEmit` clean, `pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force` → 4/4 clean. Real SSR checks: `/settings/academic-calendar` and `/wallet` → real `200`s, no error markers; the exact student page from the bug report (`/students/019fa731-684f-7e75-b4c6-49a063c19a4b`) → real `200`, no error markers (a raw HTTP check can't exercise the client-side query that was actually broken — no browser automation tool available, the same honestly-flagged gap every prior slice in this file states — verification here rests on the confirmed-identical fix pattern already proven correct for `getMySession()`, plus `WalletCard`'s own already-correct `null`-handling logic, plus a clean compile). No backend changes, no contracts regen needed — `apps/api`/`apps/worker` untouched throughout, `apps/web` picked up both changes via ordinary dev-server hot reload. No new frontend or backend files — both fixes are edits to existing files only.

## Slice 12 (Part A — Wallet-Funded Receipts Backend) — 2026-08-05

**Verdict: built and verified genuinely end-to-end against the live stack, with the exact financial-correctness risk this dispatch exists to close (a wallet-funded receipt reusing/double-posting a GL journal, so reversing it would silently desync the wallet from the ledger) directly demonstrated closed** — a real multi-invoice wallet sweep, a real single-invoice `transferToFees()` call, a real above-threshold approval round trip, and a real attempted reversal that is correctly rejected, all cross-checked directly against Postgres, not just API-response trust. One real bug was found and fixed by this dispatch's own new Jest specs before ever reaching a live run — see below.

### What was built

**1. Migration `0233-make-pay-receipt-journal-id-nullable.ts`** — `ALTER TABLE app.pay_receipt ALTER COLUMN journal_id DROP NOT NULL`, FK (`ON DELETE RESTRICT`) left exactly as-is (a `NULL` FK column is simply exempt from FK enforcement — no constraint edit needed). `PayReceiptEntity.journalId` typed `string | null`, `@Column` `nullable: true`, `journal` relation `nullable: true`. `ReceiptResponseDto.journalId` (`receipt.dto.ts`) updated to `string | null`/`nullable: true` — confirmed via the live `GET /api/docs-json` fetch that its generated schema now reads `{"type":"object","format":"uuid","nullable":true}`, the IDENTICAL shape this codebase's own pre-existing `reversalOfId`/`sessionId` nullable-uuid fields already produce (a known, pre-existing `@nestjs/swagger` codegen quirk for nullable uuid properties without an explicit `type: String`, not a new problem). **Reporting-query sweep performed before writing the migration** (per the dispatch's own explicit instruction, not assumed safe): grepped every `journalId`/`journal_id` reference across `domains/payments` and `domains/reporting` — `receipts-register.report.ts`/`fee-collection.report.ts`/`mv_daily_collections` (migration `0160`) all read `pay_receipt`/`pay_receipt_split` directly with **no join to `gl_journal` at all**; `general-ledger.report.ts` reads `gl_journal_line` directly with **no join back to `pay_receipt`** either (confirmed via `Grep` — zero matches for `pay_receipt` in that file). No other file anywhere in `packages/server/src` dereferences `PayReceiptEntity.journal`/`.journalId` in a way that assumes non-null. No fix was needed anywhere outside the migration + entity/DTO type changes.

**2. `ReceiptsService.recordWalletFundedReceipt(em, {studentId, payerName, receiptDate, allocations, cashierId, walletTransactionId})`** (`receipts.service.ts`) — creates exactly ONE `pay_receipt` (`journalId: null`, `status: 'POSTED'`, `total` = Σallocations), ONE `pay_receipt_split` (`method: 'WALLET'`, `amount` = total), and one `pay_receipt_allocation` row per allocation (`toPrepayment: false` always — a wallet sweep only ever applies up to what's owed, never overpays). Reuses `captureReceipt()`'s own real numbering (`NumberingService.allocate(em, RECEIPT_DOC_TYPE)`, the same `PAY-######` series — not a separate one) and its exact `balance_after` convention (`computeBalanceAfterCredit()` — prior running student-ledger balance minus total). **Does NOT call `PostingService.post()`** (the caller already posted the real GL journal) and **does NOT touch `bill_invoice`/`bill_installment`** (the caller already applied those). **Judgement call, documented in the code**: DOES append one `std_ledger_entry` via `StudentLedgerService.appendEntry()`, mirroring `captureReceipt()`'s own step — judged cheap (one extra insert, no other side effect) and necessary for correctness (omitting it would leave the student's own statement silently missing a real payment every other funding method always records, a worse and more surprising gap than the row costs).

**3. `WalletTransactionsService.sweepToInvoices(em, {walletId, invoiceIds, approvalRef?, actorId})`** (`wallet-transactions.service.ts`) — locks the wallet, computes `availableBalance = wallet.balance + wallet.overdraftLimit` (not `balance` alone — correctly lets an overdraft-enabled wallet use its real remaining capacity, consistent with `assertFloor()`'s own invariant every debit path here already enforces), then loops the caller-ordered `invoiceIds`, applying `take = min(remainingBalance, invoice.balance)` per invoice via the existing private `applyInvoiceAllocation()`, skipping invoices already at zero balance. **A real safety check with no precedent in `transferToFees()`** (which trusts its single caller-given `invoiceId` unchecked): each invoice's own `studentId` is verified to match `wallet.studentId` before any allocation runs, rejecting outright if not — a caller bug threading the wrong invoice id into a multi-invoice list must never debit one student's wallet into a different student's invoice. Posts exactly ONE aggregated GL journal (debit `WALLET`, credit `AR_STUDENT`, for the TOTAL actually swept) and inserts exactly ONE `wall_transaction` row (`type: 'FEE_TRANSFER'`) — never one per invoice. Applies the SAME `assertBelowThresholdOrApproved()` gate `transferToFees()` uses, against the aggregate total. Returns `{totalSwept, allocations, receiptId, transactionId, shortfall}` — `shortfall` lists every invoice still owing money after the sweep (whether never reached at all, or only partially covered), computed from each invoice's balance captured **before** `applyInvoiceAllocation()` mutates it in place (see "the one real bug" below). Returns a clean `{totalSwept: 0, ...}` result — no journal, no transaction, no receipt — when nothing was actually swept, rather than a degenerate zero-amount posting.

**Deliberate, documented deviation from the task brief's own literal signature**: `sweepToInvoices()`'s input adds an `approvalRef?: string | null` field the brief's own `{walletId, invoiceIds, actorId}` shape doesn't list — added because the SAME brief also explicitly requires this method to enforce the threshold-approval gate (and verification item 4 explicitly requires proving an above-threshold sweep can be approved and then succeed), and a gate with no way to ever supply a valid `approvalRef` would make a legitimately-approved large sweep permanently impossible to complete. No new `POST .../sweep-to-invoices/request` endpoint was added either — `dto.approvalRef` verifies against the SAME `WALLET_TRANSFER_ENTITY_TYPE` + wallet id the pre-existing `POST .../transfer-to-fees/request` endpoint already submits approval instances for (`ApprovalEngineService.getStatus()` resolves the latest instance for a given `(entityType, entityId)` pair with no further scoping — an instance submitted via the existing endpoint is equally valid for either execute path). Verified live end-to-end (see Verification item 4).

**4. `transferToFees()` extended, strictly additively** — after its own pre-existing logic succeeds byte-for-byte unchanged (idempotency replay, threshold gate, floor checks, GL posting, invoice allocation, `wall_transaction` insert), it now also calls a new shared private helper `attachWalletFundedReceipt()` (looks up the student's name via a newly-injected `StdStudentRepository`, calls `ReceiptsService.recordWalletFundedReceipt()`, then cross-references the just-inserted `wall_transaction.receipt_id` via a new `WallTransactionRepository.updateReceiptId()` — a plain targeted `UPDATE`, not a stale-entity `.save()`, since `wall_transaction` carries no immutability trigger unlike `pay_receipt`). `sweepToInvoices()` calls the same shared helper. `WalletTransactionsService` gained two new constructor dependencies, both appended at the END of the existing param list (not interleaved) to keep every pre-existing positional `new WalletTransactionsService(...)` call — real code and every prior test file — valid with only an append: `StdStudentRepository`, `ReceiptsService`. No module-wiring change was needed: `WalletModule` already imports `PaymentsModule`, which already provides/exports `ReceiptsService`; `domains/wallet` <-> `domains/payments` is already bidirectionally sanctioned in `module-deps.json` (confirmed by reading the real file before relying on it, not assumed).

**5. `POST /wallets/:id/sweep-to-invoices`** (`wallet-transactions.controller.ts`) — `{invoiceIds: string[], approvalRef?: string}` body (`SweepToInvoicesDto`), same `wallet:transaction:transfer` permission `transferToFees()`/`transferToWallet()` already use (confirmed the exact code by reading the controller, not assumed). Real `SweepToInvoicesResponseDto` (`totalSwept`, `allocations[]`, `receiptId`, `transactionId`, `shortfall[]`, every `Money` field a decimal string).

**6. Reversal guard** — `ReceiptsService.reverseReceipt()` gains a check immediately after loading the original receipt's splits (before allocations are loaded, before any unwind/GL-reverse/contra-receipt logic runs): if any split's `method` is in a new exported `NON_REVERSIBLE_RECEIPT_SPLIT_METHODS` constant (`readonly string[]`, currently `["WALLET", "CREDIT_BALANCE"]` — deliberately a plain string array, not `readonly PayReceiptSplitMethod[]`, since `"CREDIT_BALANCE"` isn't a real split-method value yet, so Part D can append it without touching this guard at all), throws a `ValidationException` with **exactly** the specified message. A second, defense-in-depth check immediately follows: if `original.journalId` is `null` (which, by construction, only a WALLET/CREDIT_BALANCE-funded receipt ever is, and is always already rejected by the guard above), throws explicitly rather than reaching `PostingService.reverse()` with a non-null assertion — this also gives TypeScript a real narrowed `string` for that call, not an `!`-asserted one.

### The one real bug found and fixed — caught by this dispatch's own new Jest spec, never shipped

`sweepToInvoices()`'s original draft computed each invoice's `shortfall.remainingBalance` as `invoice.balance.subtract(take)` **after** calling `applyInvoiceAllocation()` — but that private helper mutates `invoice.balance` **in place** on the same entity instance the loop iteration holds (`invoice.balance = invoice.balance.subtract(amount)`), so the "after" read was silently reading the already-decremented value, computing `2000 - 2000 = 0` instead of the real `4000 - 2000 = 2000`. Caught immediately by the new `wallet-transactions.service.spec.ts` "stops mid-list" test (`expect(result.shortfall).toEqual([{invoiceId: 'invoice-2', remainingBalance: Money.fromInt(2000)}])` failed with an empty array on the first run) — fixed by capturing `balanceBeforeSweep = invoice.balance` immediately after the invoice loads, before `applyInvoiceAllocation()` ever runs, and computing `stillOwed` from that captured value. Documented inline in the fix itself so a future reader of this same private-helper's mutate-in-place behavior doesn't reintroduce the same class of bug elsewhere.

### Contracts regen sequence followed exactly

`pnpm --filter @klickit/server run build` (clean) → stopped `apps/api`'s process tree (PIDs `6344`/`22356`) → restarted (`pnpm --filter @klickit/api run start:dev`, new PID `12588`) → confirmed clean boot (`Nest application successfully started`, `Mapped {/api/v1/wallets/:id/sweep-to-invoices, POST} route`) → `GET /health` → `{"status":"ok"}` → fetched the LIVE `GET /api/docs-json` fresh → confirmed `/api/v1/wallets/{id}/sweep-to-invoices`'s `post` operation present AND `ReceiptResponseDto.journalId` now `nullable: true` BEFORE regenerating → `pnpm --filter contracts run generate` → **451 DTO classes, 2212 properties translated** (up from Slice 11 Part 2's 447/2201 baseline — 4 new DTO classes: `SweepToInvoicesDto`/`SweepToInvoicesResponseDto`/`SweepToInvoicesAllocationResponseDto`/`SweepToInvoicesShortfallResponseDto`), same 16 pre-existing duplicate-`operationId` disambiguations, unchanged → `pnpm --filter contracts run build` clean → `pnpm --filter contracts exec jest --maxWorkers=2` → **903/903 passing** (up from 895).

### Verification — real, live, direct `psql` cross-checks throughout (no browser automation available, same honestly-flagged gap every prior slice states — not applicable here anyway, Part A is backend-only)

A throwaway `apps/api/src/verify-slice12-parta-mint-user.ts` (`NestFactory.createApplicationContext(AppModule)` only, to mint 2 real throwaway users — an initiator and a decider, since BR-APPR-01 blocks self-approval — both granted the real seeded `System Admin` role, `process.exit(0)` on every path, closed immediately after; independently confirmed via `Get-NetTCPConnection` that `apps/api` itself was unaffected and still the correct PID both before and after each run) backed a separate, plain PowerShell script issuing real `Invoke-RestMethod` calls against the already-running `apps/api` on port 3000 — every actual assertion a real HTTP round trip, cross-checked directly against Postgres via `docker exec klickiterp-postgres-1 psql`.

1. **Real student + wallet + 2 invoices, sweep in due-date order** — student `Slice12PartA Verify` created via real `POST /students`; wallet via real `POST /wallets/students/:id`; topped up to `5000.0000` via real `POST /wallets/:id/topup`; 2 real `bill_invoice` rows inserted directly (`3000.0000` due `2026-08-10`, `4000.0000` due `2026-08-20` — matching this codebase's own `wallet-e2e.integration.spec.ts` precedent for constructing real, constraint-satisfying invoice fixtures without needing the full fee-structure/billing UI flow, since `trg_bill_installments_sum` only fires on `bill_installment` writes and never fires at all when zero installment rows exist for an invoice). `POST /wallets/:id/sweep-to-invoices` with both ids in due-date order → real `totalSwept: "5000.0000"`, `allocations: [{invoice1, 3000.0000}, {invoice2, 2000.0000}]`, `shortfall: [{invoice2, remainingBalance: "2000.0000"}]`. **Direct `psql` cross-checks, all confirmed**: `wall_wallet.balance = 0.0000`, invoice1 `balance=0.0000, status=PAID`, invoice2 `balance=2000.0000, status=PARTIALLY_PAID` (exactly `2000.0000` of it, as specified); one `pay_receipt` row (`journal_id` genuinely `NULL`, `total=5000.0000`, `status=POSTED`); exactly ONE `pay_receipt_split` (`method=WALLET`, `amount=5000.0000`); exactly TWO `pay_receipt_allocation` rows (`3000.0000`→invoice1, `2000.0000`→invoice2, both `to_prepayment=false`); the `wall_transaction` row for this sweep (`type=FEE_TRANSFER`) has its real `receipt_id` correctly pointing at the new receipt. **The GL journal, specifically checked for the exact risk this dispatch exists to close**: joined `wall_transaction.journal_id` → `gl_journal_line` directly → exactly **2 lines under ONE journal id** — debit `2030` (WALLET) `5000.0000`, credit `1100` (AR_STUDENT) `5000.0000` — confirmed genuinely ONE balanced journal, not two, not reused from anywhere else.
2. **Above-threshold sweep correctly requires approval, then succeeds once approved** — topped the same wallet up to `9000.0000`, a 3rd invoice (`9000.0000`) inserted, `sweep-to-invoices` without `approvalRef` → real `422`: *"FR-WALL-013.1: ... amount 9000.0000 exceeds the KES 5000.0000 approval threshold ..."*. Submitted via the EXISTING `POST /wallets/:id/transfer-to-fees/request` endpoint (proving the reuse decision in item 3 above works for real, not just in theory) → `PENDING` instance; decided `APPROVE` by the SECOND user via `POST /approvals/instances/:id/decide` (confirming BR-APPR-01 self-approval blocking is real — the first user could not have decided their own submission) → `APPROVED`; `sweep-to-invoices` retried WITH `approvalRef` → real `totalSwept: "9000.0000"`, `shortfall: []`, invoice3 fully `PAID`.
3. **`transferToFees()` (existing single-invoice endpoint) now also produces a real receipt, everything else unchanged** — topped up `500.0000`, invoice4 (`500.0000`) inserted, `POST /wallets/:id/transfer-to-fees {amount:500, invoiceId}` → real `201`, `receiptId` populated (previously always `null`), `journalId` populated (the wallet transaction's own real journal, unaffected). **Direct `psql` cross-check**: the new `pay_receipt` row — `journal_id IS NULL`, `total=500.0000`, `status=POSTED` — confirming a wallet-funded receipt via the pre-existing single-invoice path is structurally identical to one via the new multi-invoice sweep path.
4. **Reversal guard — the core reason this dispatch exists** — submitted + approved (2nd user) a `PAYMENT_REVERSALS` instance for the `transferToFees()` receipt from item 3, then called the real `POST /payments/receipts/:id/reverse` → real `422`, message **byte-for-byte**: *"This receipt was funded from the student's wallet/credit balance and can't be reversed here — it would restore the ledger but not the wallet/credit balance. Contact an administrator for a manual correction."* **Regression check — an ORDINARY receipt still reverses completely normally**: opened a real cashier session (`POST /payments/sessions/open`), captured a real CASH receipt (`POST /payments/receipts`, `250.0000` against a 5th real invoice), submitted + approved + executed its own reversal via the exact same 3-step dance → real success: `status: "POSTED"` (the new contra), `reversalOfId` pointing at the original. **Direct `psql` cross-check**: the original CASH receipt's own row now shows `status=REVERSED`, a real non-null `journal_id` — confirming the guard rejects WALLET-funded receipts specifically and does not over-match ordinary ones.
5. **`pnpm --filter server exec tsc --noEmit`** → clean. **`pnpm exec jest wallet payments --maxWorkers=2`** (from `packages/server`) → **16 suites, 158 tests, all passing** (including the new/extended specs: `recordWalletFundedReceipt()`'s split/allocation-sum-equals-total assertions, `sweepToInvoices()`'s mid-list-stop + threshold + shortfall/receipt-cross-reference tests, the reversal guard firing for WALLET and NOT firing for CASH, `transferToFees()`'s 3 new tests confirming its pre-existing behavior is unchanged AND it now produces a receipt — zero regressions across the whole wallet/payments surface). **`pnpm turbo run typecheck lint --filter=@klickit/web --force`** → **4/4 clean** (contracts types changed; no frontend code touched this pass, Part B's job).
6. **A real, pre-existing test fragility found and fixed while making `wallet-e2e.integration.spec.ts` pass again, not caused by this pass's own logic**: that pre-existing integration test's own "GL WALLET control account nets to zero" assertion checks the ENTIRE shared control account, not just this test's own postings — a real, direct `psql` query confirmed this dev DB now carries 3 genuinely real, unrelated `ACTIVE` wall_wallet rows (balances `12300`/`1100`/`1000`, residue from OTHER slices' own verification work, confirmed NOT created by this pass) plus a real `800.0000` of orphaned-but-permanent `gl_journal_line` residue from this dispatch's OWN first debugging attempt (a topup+spend sequence that committed to the DB before the `pay_receipt.journal_id` migration had been applied — the enclosing wallet/transaction rows were cleaned up by the test's own `finally` block, but `gl_journal_line` is immutable by design, so those 2 lines are permanent, uniquely-suffixed residue, the same class this test's own file already documents for `gl_account`/`gl_period`/`gl_fiscal_year`). The assertion's own "whole account nets to zero" precondition is no longer generally true in this shared dev DB — fixed by making the check DELTA-based (capture the account's balance immediately before this test's own top-up/spend/transfer sequence runs, assert it's unchanged afterward) rather than assuming zero — a strictly more correct, ambient-state-robust check that still verifies the exact same real invariant (this test's own 3 postings net to zero: `+1000 -200 -800 = 0`).

## Slice 12 (Part B — Frontend Wallet-Sweep Integration) — 2026-08-05

**Verdict: built and verified genuinely end-to-end against the live stack — real invoices generated via the real bulk-generate endpoint, a real wallet swept across them in caller-order via the new `sweepToInvoices()` endpoint, and every resulting UI-facing value (settled amounts, shortfall, receipt id) cross-checked directly against Postgres.** Contracts were already current from Part A (confirmed — no regen needed, see below). A real, previously-latent ordering bug was found and fixed by this dispatch: `BulkAdhocInvoicesService.generateForStudent()`'s returned `invoiceIds` are **not** reliably due-date ordered, and a live test proved it — see "Real finding" below.

### What was built

**1. `apps/web/src/features/wallet/api/wallets.api.ts`** — added `sweepToInvoices(walletId, {invoiceIds, approvalRef?})`, placed immediately after `transferToFees()`, wrapping `POST /wallets/{id}/sweep-to-invoices`. Response mapping: every invoice in `allocations` gets a `"settled"` outcome (real swept amount + receipt id); every invoice in `shortfall` gets a new, distinct `"partialShortfall"` outcome (real remaining balance) — an invoice can legitimately get BOTH in the same run (partially covered), so outcome list items are keyed on `${invoiceId}-${outcome}`, not `invoiceId` alone. A thrown error (`isTransferNeedsApprovalError`/`isInsufficientBalanceError`/generic) marks ALL of that student's invoices with the same outcome kind, since the whole aggregate call failed. That is UNCHANGED when the wallet checkbox is off. When it's ON, the dialog now stays open even for a single invoice and shows the real sweep outcome in place before the user moves on — an immediate redirect would otherwise race the sweep call and hide its result from the one place the user is already looking. Added a `singleInvoiceDescription`/`viewInvoiceLinkSingle` pair of keys so the pre-existing `multiInvoiceDescription` copy ("categories have different due dates, so N invoices were generated") isn't shown incorrectly for the new single-invoice-but-still-open case.

Reading `BulkAdhocInvoicesService.generateForStudent()` (per the dispatch's own instruction to confirm this) showed its due-date grouping is built from `BillFeeStructureLineRepository.listByStructureAndTerm()`, a plain `.find()` with **no `ORDER BY` clause** — so the array order `result.succeeded[].invoiceIds` comes back in is not guaranteed to be due-date order. Rather than trust it, both components now fetch each invoice's real `dueDate` (`getInvoice()`, already imported) and sort ascending before ever calling `sweepToInvoices()`. **This was proven necessary live, not just theoretically** — see below.

Real Swahili and French translations were written for every new key.

**Real, unplanned finding — sw.json/fr.json are NOT actually translated**: while adding these keys, a direct byte comparison (`Get-Content -Raw`, both files against `en.json`) showed `sw.json` and `fr.json` are **byte-for-byte identical to `en.json`** — every single existing key in both files is plain English text, not Swahili/French. This pass added genuine Swahili/French translations for every NEW key it introduced (not English placeholders), but did not attempt to fix the pre-existing, apparently-total translation gap across the rest of either file — that's a real, separate, much larger finding outside this dispatch's scope, flagged here for visibility rather than silently worked around.

## Slice 12 (Part C — Duplicate Fee-Category-Per-Term Guard) — 2026-08-05

**Verdict: built and verified genuinely end-to-end against the live stack — a real student already billed for "Swimming" this term (pre-existing data, not seeded by this pass) was bulk-generated against Swimming + a new category in one call, correctly split into a real new invoice for only the new category plus `alreadyBilledCategoryIds` on the success entry; a follow-up call selecting ONLY Swimming again landed entirely in `skipped[]` with zero new invoices — both cross-checked directly against Postgres.** A real debit note re-billing the same already-billed Swimming category was also created and posted successfully, confirming `DebitNotesService` (and by the same code path, `LateFeeBatchesService`) are completely unaffected by this guard, exactly as designed.

### The one real design decision — how full-skip vs. partial-skip vs. failure are signaled

`BulkAdhocInvoicesService.generateForStudent()` was changed from throwing-only to returning a **discriminated union**, `GenerateForStudentResult = {kind:"generated", invoiceIds, alreadyBilledCategoryIds} | {kind:"skipped", alreadyBilledCategoryIds}`, rather than introducing a new exception subclass for the full-skip case. Reasoning: `bulkGenerate()`'s existing try/catch around `generateForStudent()` exists purely to catch genuine failures (`NotFoundException` — no applicable PUBLISHED structure; `ValidationException` — none of the selected categories appear on the structure at all) that legitimately belong in `failed[]`. A full duplicate-billing skip is not an error — nothing went wrong, the student simply doesn't need re-billing — so modeling it as a thrown exception the caller would need to specifically catch-and-not-treat-as-an-error would be modeling a normal outcome as an abnormal control-flow path. A return-value discriminant instead lets `bulkGenerate()`'s routing logic be a plain `if (result.kind === "skipped")` check sitting naturally alongside the untouched try/catch, and keeps the exception vocabulary reserved for what actually failed. The PARTIAL-skip case (some but not all selected categories already billed) is not a separate discriminant arm — it's the ordinary `"generated"` arm with a non-empty `alreadyBilledCategoryIds` riding along, since a partial skip really is a success from the caller's point of view (the student got billed for what was still owed); `bulkGenerate()` only promotes `alreadyBilledCategoryIds` onto the `BulkAdhocGenerateSuccess` entry when it's non-empty, keeping the common (nothing skipped) case's shape exactly as it always was.

### What was built (backend)

**1. `BillInvoiceLineRepository.listAlreadyBilledCategoryIds(studentId, termId, feeCategoryIds, manager?)`** (`bill-invoice-line.repository.ts`) — joins `bill_invoice_line` → `bill_invoice` via the entity's existing `invoice` relation (`createQueryBuilder().innerJoin("line.invoice", "invoice")`), filtering `fee_category_id IN (...)`, `student_id`, `term_id`, `status <> 'VOID'`, returning the subset of the GIVEN category ids the student already has a real (non-VOID) line for. **Verified, not assumed, which TypeORM `where`/`select` form this codebase's `BillInvoiceRepository` siblings actually use**: raw snake_case column-name form throughout (`line.fee_category_id`, `invoice.student_id`, not `line.feeCategoryId`/`invoice.studentId`) — matching `findOpenForStudent()`/`findOverdueOpen()`/`findAllOpen()`'s own established convention in this exact file's sibling repository, whose own `findOpenPaginated()` doc comment already documents that property-path form is only ever REQUIRED (and tested) inside `.orderBy()` when combined with `skip()`/`take()` and a join — not applicable here. `.innerJoin("line.invoice", "invoice")` itself still correctly uses property-path form — relation-join specs are a separate, always-property-path TypeORM API, same as this sibling file's own `.leftJoinAndSelect("invoice.student", ...)`.

**2. `BulkAdhocInvoicesService`** (`bulk-adhoc-invoices.service.ts`) — gained a 6th constructor param, `BillInvoiceLineRepository`, appended at the END of the existing param list (both real DI — `billing.module.ts` already registers/exports `BillInvoiceLineRepository`, confirmed, no wiring change needed — and the test spec's positional `new BulkAdhocInvoicesService(...)` call). `generateForStudent()`: right after `matchedLines` is computed and validated non-empty (the pre-existing "none matched the structure" guard, UNCHANGED — still throws `ValidationException`), the matched categories are checked against `listAlreadyBilledCategoryIds()`; `matchedLines` is split into `billableLines` (fed to the UNCHANGED due-date-grouping/generate/post logic) and `alreadyBilledCategoryIds`. Zero `billableLines` → returns the `"skipped"` discriminant. `bulkGenerate()` routes `"skipped"` results into a new `skipped: BulkAdhocGenerateSkip[]` array (distinct from `failed[]`) and attaches non-empty `alreadyBilledCategoryIds` onto `BulkAdhocGenerateSuccess` entries for the partial case. Class doc comment rewritten: the prior "No DB-level duplicate-submit guard" gap note is replaced with a full description of the new guard, explicitly re-affirming it's still an application-level check (not new DDL) and still doesn't close a true concurrent-double-submit race — narrowed from "any repeat submission" to that one specific remaining window, same mitigation (disabled-while-submitting frontend button) as before.

**3. DTO/controller threading** (`bulk-adhoc-invoice.dto.ts`) — new `BulkAdhocInvoiceSkipDto {studentId, alreadyBilledCategoryIds}`; `BulkAdhocInvoiceSuccessDto` gained `alreadyBilledCategoryIds?: string[]` (`@ApiPropertyOptional({type:[String]})`, matching this domain's own `bulk-billing.dto.ts` precedent for optional string arrays); `BulkGenerateAdhocInvoicesResultDto` gained `skipped: BulkAdhocInvoiceSkipDto[]`. **`bulk-adhoc-invoices.controller.ts` needed NO code change** — it already returns the service's result object directly, structurally typed as the DTO (the same "structurally compatible" shape this file's own precedent already established for `succeeded`/`failed`); adding identically-named/shaped fields on both the service's `BulkAdhocGenerateResult` and the DTO kept that structural pass-through valid with zero controller edits, confirmed by a clean `tsc --noEmit`.

**4. Tests** (`bulk-adhoc-invoices.service.spec.ts`) — every pre-existing test's constructor call updated with a 6th mock (`billInvoiceLineRepository.listAlreadyBilledCategoryIds` defaulted to `async () => new Set()`, i.e. "nothing already billed," so none of the pre-existing tests needed behavioral changes). New `describe("duplicate fee-category-per-term guard ...")` block, 4 new tests: full skip (all selected categories already billed → `skipped[]`, zero `generateInvoice()`/`postInvoice()` calls, and an explicit assertion that the repository call itself is scoped to the matched categories/student/term); partial skip (one of two selected categories already billed → exactly one `generateInvoice()` call carrying ONLY the still-billable category's line, `alreadyBilledCategoryIds` on the success entry); regression (a genuinely new, never-billed category still generates normally with NO `alreadyBilledCategoryIds` key present at all — `not.toHaveProperty()`, not just an empty array, confirming the field is truly omitted in the common case); and a mixed-batch test (one student fully skipped, another genuinely succeeding, in the same `bulkGenerate()` call — confirms a skip never aborts the batch, mirroring this file's own pre-existing "one student's failure doesn't abort the batch" test).

### What was built (frontend)

**`bulk-generate-invoice-form.tsx`** — `GenerateSummary` gained `skipped`/`partiallySkipped` arrays (the latter derived client-side from `result.succeeded[].alreadyBilledCategoryIds`); new `formatCategoryNames()` helper resolves category ids to real names via the SAME `categoriesQuery.data` source `categoryOptions` already uses (a new `categoryNameById` memo), never showing raw UUIDs. Results Card gained two new sections alongside the existing `resultFailedTitle` block: `resultSkippedTitle` (full skips, distinct list) and `resultPartialSkipTitle` (students who succeeded but had some categories skipped) — the top summary `<Alert>` variant now also turns `"warning"` when `skipped.length > 0`, not just on `failed.length > 0`.

**`generate-invoice-dialog.tsx`** — since this dialog only ever submits one `studentId`, a full skip means `result.skipped.length > 0` (at most one entry) and is now handled BEFORE the old fall-through-to-empty-invoice-list path: a new `skippedNotice` state renders a dedicated warning `<Alert>` in place of the categories form, with just a Close button in the footer (no wallet processing possible — nothing was generated). A partial skip (`result.succeeded[0].alreadyBilledCategoryIds` non-empty) sets `partialSkipCategoryIds`, rendered as a second warning `<Alert>` alongside the existing generated-invoices success `<Alert>`. **One real interaction fix caught while wiring this**: the pre-existing "wallet checkbox OFF + exactly one invoice → instant redirect to `/billing/invoices/{id}`" shortcut had to be narrowed to also require `alreadyBilledCategoryIds.length === 0` — otherwise a partial-skip single-invoice generation would redirect away before the user ever saw the "some categories were already billed" note, silently hiding exactly the information this guard exists to surface.

**i18n** — 4 new keys per namespace (`billing.bulkGenerate.{resultSkippedTitle,resultSkippedEntry,resultPartialSkipTitle,resultPartialSkipEntry}`, `billing.invoices.generateDialog.{alreadyBilledSkippedNotice,alreadyBilledPartialSkipNotice}`) added to `en.json`/`sw.json`/`fr.json`, with genuine Swahili and French translations written for every one (not English copies) — matching Part A/B's own per-dispatch discipline; the wider pre-existing sw.json/fr.json translation gap Part B already flagged was left untouched, out of scope here.
